newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bandai chief to quit on June 27 over failed merger.
newsitem.headline: Bandai chief to quit on June 27 over failed merger.

text.p: Japanese toymaker Bandai Co Ltd announced on Thursday that its president, Makoto Yamashina, will resign from his current post as of June 27, following the company's failed merger with Sega Enterprises Ltd.

Bandai said in a statement that, while giving up the presidency, Yamashina will stay on with the company as chairman. Takashi Mogi, current president of three Bandai units, will become the company's new president, it said.
Six directors and two auditors will also step down from their current posts, Bandai said.

On Tuesday, just a day before Bandai and Sega were due to sign a merger contract, they announced that they had called off the deal after strong opposition from mid-level Bandai managers. They said they would instead pursue a tie-up in product merchandising and development.
The bungled merger tarnished the credibility of Bandai's top management, who were unable to quell dissent within the company over the plan, and pushed down the company's shares.
On the Tokyo bourse on Thursday, Bandai shares extended their recent losses, dropping 120 yen to 2,550 yen as of 0404 GMT.
Bandai, Japan's top toy maker, was founded in 1950 by the incumbent president Makoto Yamashina's father, Naoharu Yamashina.

Sega, maker of the Saturn 32-bit video-game player, and Bandai, known for its Power Rangers series and virtual pet toy "Tamagotchi", said in January that they would merge to create a global entertainment giant rivalling Walt Disney Co of the United States.
